claim: Header TR (pixdim[4]) of the preprocessed files
method: nibabel header zooms[3], all scans

claim: RepetitionTime in raw-scan bold.json sidecars
method: read 227 sidecars

claim: Scanner trigger spacing in physio recording (1 participant)
method: rising edges of 'trigger' column at 1000 Hz
value: 657 triggers; interval median 1.4000 s, min 1.4000, max 1.4000

claim: Time points per scan = acquired volumes - 5 dropped
method: header dim[4]

claim: Usable scan duration
Volumes after resampling to 2 s (as Brain-JEPA training data)
Header fields identical across scans
method: compare shape/zooms/affine/datatype/descrip/q-sform
value: {"shape": true, "zooms": true, "affine": true, "datatype": true, "descrip": true, "qform_code": true, "sform_code": true}

claim: Grid is the standard FSL MNI152 2 mm grid
No slice-timing info and no scaling in header
method: slice_duration, toffset, scl_slope

claim: No NaN or Inf values
method: count over all voxels and volumes

claim: Every voxel time series is mean-centred
method: max |temporal mean| over brain voxels

claim: Voxel temporal std is about 1 (variance-normalised)
method: median of voxel std, brain-like voxels
value: medians 0.866 to 0.904; share of voxels with std 0.8-1.2: 0.684 to 0.819

claim: Signal distribution is near-Gaussian per voxel
method: median skew / excess kurtosis of 30k voxels

claim: Std is lower at the brain edge than inside (z-scoring happened before the MNI warp, which averages voxels)
method: median voxel std within 2 voxels of the mask edge vs >= 6 voxels inside

claim: Value range
method: min / max over brain voxels

claim: Voxels with any signal split into near-empty and brain-like groups
method: voxel std histogram; brain-like = std > 0.4
value: near-empty share 0.450 to 0.489; voxels in the 0.2-0.4 gap 5898-7834

claim: Brain-like voxels per scan
method: count std > 0.4

claim: Masks overlap across people
method: pairwise Dice

claim: Share of signal power below / inside / above 0.01-0.1 Hz (TR 1.4 s)
method: FFT of 20k voxels per scan
value: below 0.20 to 0.32; inside 0.68 to 0.79; above 0.0008 to 0.0032
expected: not a sharp band: the pipeline uses a soft Gaussian filter (fslmaths -bptf), see E4

claim: Peak frequency and 99%-power frequency
method: argmax / cumulative 99% of mean spectrum
value: peak 0.0055 to 0.0197 Hz; 99% of power below 0.056 to 0.062 Hz

claim: Power above 0.1 Hz is removed
method: share of power above 0.1 Hz

claim: Spectrum shape is explained by the pipeline's Gaussian band-pass (sigma 5 s low-pass, 50 s high-pass)
method: spread (log10 range) of the mean spectrum over 0.012-0.08 Hz, before vs after dividing by the filter's power response
value: raw spread 2.72 decades; after removing filter 0.18 decades; low-pass half-power at 0.0265 Hz

claim: Low-pass width fitted from the data matches the pipeline setting: sigma = 1/(2*TR*0.1) volumes = 3.57 vol = 5 s with TR 1.4 (it would be 5 vol = 7 s if TR 1.0 had been used)
method: grid search 2-10 s: Gaussian low-pass width that leaves the flattest residual (log-log line removed, 1/f allowed), 0.012-0.08 Hz
value: best fit 4.7 s; residual 0.018 (best), 0.037 at 5 s, 0.348 at 7 s

claim: Column layout: 6 unit-norm + 6 params + 6 first differences + one-hot flags + 3 trends
method: unit norm, zero mean, corr(diff(c7-12), c13-18), one-hot test, constant/linear test, ncol = 21 + flags
value: all 159 files: unit-norm True, diff corr min 1.0000, one-hot True, trends True, count rule True

claim: Columns 10-12 are translations in mm: they reproduce the pipeline's MeanFD (QC PDF)
method: mean over frames of sum |diff| of columns 10-12 vs MeanFD printed in QC PDF
value: 10 people; max abs difference 0.0007 mm; r = 1.0000

claim: Pipeline MeanFD ignores rotations; Power FD (rotations at 50 mm) is higher
method: Power FD mean vs pipeline MeanFD (translations only, recomputed = QC PDF value, see F2)
value: Power FD 0.075 to 0.586 vs pipeline-style 0.051 to 0.506 mm (all 159); Power FD higher in 159/159

claim: Motion columns were not high-pass filtered (any high-pass removes the mean)
method: max |mean| of translation columns 10-12 per person; share of translation power above 0.1 Hz (info)
value: max |mean| 0.032 to 2.276 mm; power above 0.1 Hz 0.00 to 0.62

claim: Flagged (outlier) volumes per scan
method: number of one-hot columns
value: median 4, range 0-29; 15 scans with none; 2 with more than 20

claim: Global signal is smooth
method: lag-1 autocorrelation of global signal

claim: Global signal explains little of each voxel
method: median r^2 between voxel and global signal

claim: First 30 volumes change more than the rest (edge effect)
method: median DVARS first 30 / rest
value: ratio 0.78 to 1.37 (median 0.97); higher in 19 of 159 scans

claim: Neighbouring voxels are correlated (spatial smoothness)
method: mean corr of voxel with +x neighbour (2 mm)

claim: Implied smoothness (Gaussian approximation)
method: FWHM = 2.355 * d / sqrt(-4 ln r), d = 2 mm

claim: Mirror (left-right) voxels correlate more than same-distance controls
method: mean corr homotopic pairs minus y-shifted pairs at the same distance; sign test over people
value: difference 0.035 to 0.104; positive in 159/159 (two-sided sign test p = 2.7e-48)

claim: Consistent with confounds already regressed out: own confounds explain less of the signal than other people's (main evidence is the pipeline code order)
method: median R2 over 10 mm cubes, own 21 base columns vs the median over 20 other people's columns (random sample)
value: own 0.020 to 0.105; others 0.058 to 0.088; own lower in 156/159

claim: Connectivity pattern is reproducible within a scan (first half vs second half)
method: 1730 cubes (10 mm) present in all scans; corr of Fisher-z connectivity, half 1 vs half 2
value: within-person 0.370 to 0.727 (median 0.513); between-person 0.063 to 0.444 (median 0.219); own > every other person in 159/159

claim: A person can be identified from their own connectivity ('fingerprinting')
method: for each person, is the most similar second-half matrix their own?

claim: Average connectivity strength (mean Fisher-z over all cube pairs)
method: mean of upper triangle

method: random permutation test, 10000 relabellings, n = 46 older vs 113 younger

method: random permutation test, 10000 relabellings, n = 46 older vs 113 younger

method: random permutation test, 10000 relabellings, n = 46 older vs 113 younger
